crime_highlights: the appellant was arrested with cocaine, fentanyl, and methamphetamine, each intended for trafficking
he also had a loaded handgun, primed with a round in the chamber
The appellant pled guilty to both the May and September offences
rationale_highlights: the systemic issues that may have affected [the appellant’s] family and [the appellant] himself
the impact of the Gladue factors is attenuated
she accepted that systemic issues may have played a role in bringing the appellant before the court and took that into account in imposing the sentence that she did

crime_highlights: Darren Pearce and Terrance Goodwin, both drug addicts, together stabbed Tyler Moore, a drug dealer, approximately 17 times
Mr. Pearce and Mr. Goodwin each stabbed Mr. Moore multiple times with the same knife
Mr. Moore suffered permanent injuries from the attack, including multiple stab wounds to his torso and diminished use of his left hand
rationale_highlights: he accepted that Mr. Pearce is Indigenous, and found a connection between Mr. Pearce’s heritage and his difficult background
applied to reduce Mr. Pearce’s fit sentence by one year, to four years’ imprisonment
note: Appeal decided on parity; Gladue discussed only in summary of trial judge.

crime_highlights: The complainant, who was drinking heavily, was found by two other teammates who carried her to her tent
waking up in the morning in her tent, realizing that she was naked from the waist down
the appellant had her underwear, and that he had shown it to the other men and was talking about her
rationale_highlights: the appellant’s history of negative personal experiences

but for the appellant’s unique circumstances, including Gladue considerations, the absence of a criminal record, the progress the appellant made while on bail and the length and effect of the appellant’s conditions of bail, the Crown’s requested sentence of three years would have been appropriate
note: Gladue report content never described; only effect on sentence stated.
